source: IPC-9641, High Temperature Printed Board Flatness Guideline
package_dimensions: local land area, e.g. FCBGA land
assembly_state: bare printed board during SMT build
temperature_load_history: simulated reflow profile, ambient to peak
failure_mechanism: solder joint formation defects: opens, bridging
metric: full-field flatness / dynamic warpage (ambient to reflow difference)
threshold_value: NONE - it is a test method, not a limit
reason_accepted_or_rejected: Governs the printed BOARD, not the package; references its metric to reflow temperature; contains no allowable at all. Fails package state, temperature state, metric definition and failure mechanism.

source: Warpage Analysis of Lidded Flip Chip CSP (IMAPSource)
assembly_state: package as supplied, before board attach
failure_mechanism: SMT yield: uneven solder joint formation
metric: ball-plane coplanarity (JESD22-B108B); package warpage at reflow (JESD22-B112C method)
threshold_value: 80 um coplanarity at 25 C (JEP95 Table I); -120 to +170 um warpage at 245 C reflow (SPP-024 Table II)
reason_accepted_or_rejected: Body size matches this project (21 vs 22.36 mm) but nothing else does. Package is unmounted; state is reflow or room-temperature coplanarity, not 84 C steady operation; mechanism is assembly yield, not operational reliability; metric is ball-plane coplanarity referenced ambient-to-reflow, not die-surface P-V referenced to a 25 C stress-free state. 1 of 6 admissibility conditions met.

source: Warpage in wafer-level packaging: a review of causes, modelling and mitigation (Frontiers in Electronics)
temperature_load_history: process history: mould cure, post-mould cure, cooldown
failure_mechanism: manufacturability and YIELD; handling, subsequent assembly
threshold_value: wafer < 0.5 mm for high yield; individual package max allowable 0.2 mm, 0.1 mm preferred for high yield (review citing Lau 2018b/2019b)
experimental_or_simulated: review of experimental and simulated work
reason_accepted_or_rejected: The only numeric package-level warpage allowables found anywhere in this search, but explicitly framed 'for high yields' during wafer-level packaging. Process state, not operational; total process-induced warpage, not incremental operational; mechanism is yield, not service life. The same review names 'Need for Materials Data and Failure Criteria' as an open challenge for the field.

source: Thermal Fatigue Evaluation of Pb-Free Solder Joints: Results, Lessons Learned (JOM)
package_architecture: CTBGA84 and CABGA192 chip-scale BGA on FR-4
temperature_load_history: accelerated thermal cycling, 0/100 C and other profiles, 10-min and longer dwells
failure_mechanism: solder joint thermal fatigue, daisy-chain open
threshold_value: alloy- and profile-dependent cycles-to-failure; no design allowable
applicability: REJECTED as a design constraint; RELEVANT as calibration evidence
reason_accepted_or_rejected: Correct mechanism (B) and correct assembly state, but the load is ACCELERATED THERMAL CYCLING and the output is cycles-to-failure, not a steady-state design threshold. Using it would require a discrete-joint viscoplastic model this project does not have (Sec. 3, Sec. 9), plus a field mission profile that does not exist for the reference system.

source: Thermal fatigue life of BGA solder joints made from different alloy compositions (J. Electron. Mater.)
metric: strain energy density Ed dissipated per cycle; von Mises stress; creep strain
threshold_value: comparative between alloys; no absolute allowable
applicability: REJECTED as a design constraint; RELEVANT as a metric definition
reason_accepted_or_rejected: Defines exactly the category-3 quantity that could become a category-4 allowable given a calibration, and confirms the required fidelity: creep, temperature-dependent constitutive behaviour and cyclic loading. The present M0 model has none of these and the BGA is a single homogenised elastic layer, so the metric is not computable here (Sec. 9).

source: Methodology for Predicting BGA Warpage by Incorporating Metal Layer Design (IMAPSource)
reason_accepted_or_rejected: Confirms JESD22-B112 is applied as a MEASUREMENT specification ('heaters as per JEDEC Spec JESD22B112'), not as a source of allowables. Useful only to establish what the standard is for.
